summary: Prebuilt Go binary implements a WebSocket-driven remote PTY (ccflycc.hn / cc.hn)
details: The npm package ships a single ~7MB opaque Mach-O Go binary at bin/ccfly-setup and nothing else — no source, no README, no repository field, no lifecycle scripts, no bin/main entry. The binary is a platform-specific optionalDependency intended to be resolved by a wrapper package. Its embedded module list imports github.com/creack/pty and github.com/gorilla/websocket, and it contains hardcoded destinations ws://ccflycc.hn, wss://<host>/latest.ccfly, and https://cc.hn. The combination of a pseudo-terminal library plus a WebSocket client plus a hardcoded remote endpoint is a network-driven shell: a remote party writing over the socket drives a PTY on the host running the binary. The advertised purpose in package.json is 'guided-install', which does not describe a remote-shell capability. The package has no install/postinstall hooks, so it does not execute on `npm install`; the backdoor fires when the binary is invoked (e.g., by the wrapper @ccfly/setup).

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
